steps.title: A caldera
steps.body: Santorini is a Greek island in the southern Aegean, in the Cyclades. Around 1600 BC, one of the largest volcanic eruptions in human history blew out its centre, leaving a crescent-shaped island around a flooded caldera. Vineyards cover about 1,100 hectares, on the gentle outer slopes.

steps.title: Aspa
steps.body: Santorini's soil, called aspa, is volcanic ash, pumice, lava and pieces of rock, with almost no clay or organic matter. It's very poor and drains instantly. Phylloxera can't survive in it, so vines are ungrafted and roots can be centuries old. The pumice holds a little moisture, helping roots through summer.

options: Phylloxera can't survive in volcanic aspa
steps.explanation: The volcanic soil keeps phylloxera out.

steps.title: Wind, sun and little rain
steps.body: Santorini is hot and very dry, with about 300 mm of rain a year, mostly in winter. Strong winds, including the meltemi in summer, blow constantly. Vines rely on night-time sea mist and dew for moisture. Yields are tiny, often 10 to 20 hl/ha, among the lowest in Europe.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Santorini is a crescent around a volcanic caldera
Its aspa soil keeps phylloxera out; vines are ungrafted
It's dry and windy; vines rely on sea mist
